獨立之路 (2-1-上)

THE ROAD TO INDEPENDENCE-(2-1-A)-“You just don’t understand”
課文講解重點難字發音
語速

一、課文

Reading 1

The Road to Independence

“You just don’t understand”

A 16-year-old argues when his mom tells him to be home by 10 p.m.

Another teen puts on makeup at school, so her parents won’t know.

Another just stays in her room as much as possible.

They are all looking for freedom and independence.

Reading 2

The Road to Independence

The road to independence is a challenge not only for teenagers but also for parents.

As children grow into adolescence, both must learn to adjust their roles.

Teenagers are seeking more freedom to make their own choices, while parents should be stepping back from supervision and control.

This requires trust, patience and communication.

點句子前的 🔊 或「全文朗讀」可聽發音(使用預先錄製的自然語音)。

二、講解重點

英文皆為節目講解原句。音標與中文為補充。

Reading 1

be home by (a certain time)
  • This is talking about the fact that you need to return to your house by no later than a certain time.
  • 例Your parents might say, “You must be home by 11 p.m. You have school tomorrow.”
curfew/ˈkɝfju/宵禁
  • If there’s a certain time you have to be home by every single night, we call that a curfew.
  • 例Your curfew time.
teen/tin/青少年
  • The word “teen” is short for “teenager.” And we’re talking about people between the ages of 13 and 19 years old.
as much as possible
  • That is doing something the largest amount or as often as you can.
  • 例You might try to drink water as much as possible.
They are all looking for freedom and independence.
  • These situations are just describing a situation that happens as people get older. They want more freedom, and they want more independence.
  • Kids who are younger than this, well, they need to listen to their parents. Their parents have a lot more authority over them. But as they get older, they try and test those boundaries and figure out who they are.

Reading 2

adolescence/ˌædəˈlɛsns/青春期
  • We’re talking about young people between childhood and adulthood.
  • 例Adolescents need good sleep and plenty of food as they continue to grow.
supervision/ˌsupɚˈvɪʒən/監督、看管
  • That means to watch over someone, usually to keep them safe.
  • 例As we are young, children need adult supervision. As people get older, they need less and less supervision.
step back from supervision and control
  • It’s important for parents to step back from supervision and control, but probably not completely.
  • It’s hard to find a balance between how much you need to supervise your kids and how much you need to let them be independent.
communication/kəˌmjunəˈkeʃən/溝通
  • Communication is sharing thoughts and feelings with other people.
  • 例Good communication can help families stay together and be strong.
This requires trust, patience and communication.
  • This process from being a child that needs adult supervision to being an independent adolescent requires several things: trust, patience and communication.
  • If a parent doesn’t let go enough, doesn’t give the kid independence, they can never grow up.
  • If the parent gives too much independence too fast, that child might make some really bad choices. They won’t learn enough about boundaries.

Deep Dive:step back

step back退一步、抽身
  • “Step back” means to withdraw a bit from a role, responsibility or situation, often to let others take over, to get perspective or to reduce involvement.
  • It can be literal, but we usually use it figuratively for leadership, emotions or decisions.
  • 例After leading the group project for weeks, Mia decided to step back and let her teammates finish the presentation.
  • 例Sometimes parents need to step back so their kids can learn from their own mistakes.
step up挺身而出
  • “Step up” means to take responsibility or rise to a challenge.
  • 例When the team captain got sick, Liam stepped up and led the practice perfectly.
step in介入
  • “Step in” is when someone intervenes to help or take control.
  • 例The teacher stepped in when the argument got too loud and calmed everyone down.
